`dotenvy` rejects environment variable names that start with a number (following POSIX variable naming rules).

In [`dotenvy`'s parser](file:///home/derek/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/dotenvy-0.15.7/src/parse.rs#L76-L82), a key **must start with an ASCII letter (`a-z`, `A-Z`) or an underscore (`_`)**:

```rust
if !self.line.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '_') {
    return Err(self.err());
}
```

Because `9ROUTER` starts with `9`, `dotenv()` returns `Err(LineParse("9ROUTER=...", 0))`, which `dotenv().ok()` silently ignores on line 15 of [ai.rs](file:///home/derek/projects/ryz/src/core/ai.rs#L15-L16).

### Fix

1. Rename the key in your `.env` file so it starts with a letter or underscore (e.g., `ROUTER_9=...` or `_9ROUTER=...`).
2. Update [`text`](file:///home/derek/projects/ryz/src/core/ai.rs#L16) in [ai.rs](file:///home/derek/projects/ryz/src/core/ai.rs#L16) to match:
   ```rust
   let api_key = env::var("ROUTER_9").expect("API Key not found");
   ```
3. *(Tip)* On line 56 of [`test_text`](file:///home/derek/projects/ryz/src/core/ai.rs#L56-L57), change `response.err()` to `response.as_ref().err()` so `response` isn't moved before `response.unwrap()`.
